# Residue fields over rings generated by the integers

Module `Langlands.CommutativeAlgebra.ArithmeticRegularLocalApproximation.ResidueFields`.

The base rings used in the proof of
`Langlands.CommutativeAlgebra.ArithmeticRegularLocalApproximationStatement` are quotients of
`ℤ`: the smallest subring `(⊥ : Subring Λ)` of a discrete valuation ring `Λ` (module
`Langlands.CommutativeAlgebra.ArithmeticRegularLocalApproximation.Base`). This module records
two facts about such rings `R`, expressed through the hypothesis that `Int.castRingHom R` is
surjective, i.e. every element of `R` is an integer.

## Results

- `perfectField_of_forall_eq_intCast_div`: a field `K` in which every element has the form
  `a / b` with `a b : ℤ` is a perfect field. If `K` has characteristic zero this is Mathlib's
  instance. If `K` has prime characteristic `p`, Frobenius is surjective, because
  `(a / b) = (a / b)^p` for integers `a, b` (Frobenius fixes integer casts and commutes with
  division); `PerfectRing.toPerfectField` then applies.
- `residueField_eq_intCast_div`: if every element of `R` is an integer and `𝔭` is a prime of
  `R`, every element of the residue field `𝔭.ResidueField` has the form `a / b` with
  `a b : ℤ`. The residue field is the fraction field of `R ⧸ 𝔭`
  (`IsFractionRing.div_surjective`), and every element of `R ⧸ 𝔭` is an integer.
- `perfectField_residueField`: under the same hypothesis, every residue field of `R` is a
  perfect field (the two results above combined).
- `fieldFG_of_forall_eq_div`: let `D` be a finite type `R₀`-algebra, where every element of `R₀`
  is an integer, and let `φ : D → K` be a ring map to a field such that every element of `K` is a
  quotient `φ a / φ b`. Then `K` is finitely generated as a field (`Field.FG K`). Choose a finite
  set `s` generating `D` as an `R₀`-algebra; by induction over `Algebra.adjoin` every `φ a` lies in
  the subfield generated by `φ '' s` (integers lie in every subfield), hence so does every
  quotient.

The last result is used for residue fields of localizations of finite type algebras: the
residue field of a local ring `D_𝔮` is a field of fractions of `D ⧸ 𝔮`.
